title: Conductors, Insulators and Circuit Diagrams
seo_title: Primary 5 Science: Electrical Conductors and Circuit Diagrams Worksheets (with Answers)
standard_code: Primary 5: Energy forms and uses (Electrical systems: conductors, insulators and circuit diagrams)
standard_text: Identify electrical conductors and insulators and relate their uses to electrical safety. Test whether materials conduct electricity, and draw and read circuit diagrams using symbols for batteries, bulbs, switches and wires (summary of the MOE Primary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Primary 5 science worksheets for Singapore pupils on electrical conductors and insulators, circuit testers, uses for safety, and circuit diagram symbols. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Conductors let electricity flow; insulators do not.
key_sub: Circuit diagrams use symbols for each component.
body_html:
How to think about it

Electrical conductors let electricity flow; electrical insulators do not.

  • Conductors: metals (copper, iron, aluminium, steel) and graphite.
  • Insulators: plastic, rubber, wood, glass, cloth and paper.
  • Use a circuit tester: if the bulb lights when the object is in the gap, the object is a conductor.
  • Circuit diagrams use symbols: a cell (long thin line and short thick line), a bulb (circle with a cross), a switch (gap or closed line), wires (straight lines).
Example

A steel paper clip makes the bulb in a tester light. What is it?

The bulb lit

Current flowed through the clip

Answer: A conductor.

Example

Why is a plug's case plastic but its pins metal?

Pins must conduct

The case must protect your hand

Answer: Metal conducts; plastic insulates.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all shiny things conduct. A shiny plastic button does not.
  • Thinking pencil lead is an insulator because the pencil is wood. Graphite conducts.
  • Mixing up the cell symbol and the bulb symbol.
  • Thinking water never conducts. Tap water can conduct and is dangerous near electricity.

faq.q: How do I test if a material conducts electricity?
faq.a: Put it across the gap in a circuit with a battery and a bulb. If the bulb lights, the material is a conductor.

faq.q: Why do we use symbols in circuit diagrams?
faq.a: Symbols are quick to draw and everyone understands them, so circuits can be shared and built correctly.
